# Source and translated-quotation comparison

Reviewed the complete supplied source and complete current draft, including title, standfirst, subheadings, link and publication disclosure. Applied the supplied Claims contract and quotation guidance. This report concerns source support and quotation translation only.

## Source key

The following identifiers refer to exact passages in the supplied source, not external material.

- B1: “Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party.”
- B2: “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”
- S1: “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”
- S2: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”
- S3: “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.”
- S4: “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”
- S5: “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair.”
- S6: “No comparison with another supplier is available.”
- S7: “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”
- S8: “Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions.”
- S9: “The trial lasted eight weeks.”
- S10: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered.”
- S11: “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”
- S12: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.”
- S13: “The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.”
- S14: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”
- Q0: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”
- Q1: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
- Q2: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
- Q3: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
- S15: “Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.”
- S16: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”
- S17: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.”
- S18: “All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.”

## Complete proposition accounting

Each numbered entry gives the draft passage, a standalone meaning-equivalent proposition, its precise negation with subject and scope retained, and the supplied statement excluding that negation. Repeated appearances are listed together only where they express the same proposition. Reported intentions and opinions remain statements about the named person's or team's intentions and opinions; they are not converted into objective efficacy claims. The propositions drawn from translated quotations retain their attribution to Lind.

1. **Title: “Elm Quay fick en gemensam överblick över felanmälningarna”.** Proposition: Elm Quay obtained a shared view of the repair reports in the trial. Negation: Elm Quay did not obtain a shared view of the repair reports in the trial. Support: S2 establishes the shared log and Q3 explicitly describes the customer as having one view of the reports. Together these rule out the negation. The title does not assert that the software caused a performance improvement.

2. **Standfirst: “Elm Quay Housing testade en gemensam logg för felanmälningar i två byggnader.”** Proposition: Elm Quay Housing trialled a shared repair-report log in two buildings. Negation: Elm Quay Housing did not trial a shared repair-report log in two buildings. Support: S2 identifies the trial, customer, shared log and two-building scope; S9 and S10 establish that the intended trial took place. Supported.

3. **Standfirst: “Underhållsteamet ville ge olika arbetsskift tillgång till samma information”.** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team wanted staff on different shifts to have access to the same information. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not want staff on different shifts to have access to the same information. Support: S4 states that intention. This does not claim independently measured information access or universal use. Supported.

4. **Standfirst: “utformade själva kategorierna”; subheading “Teamet utformade kategorierna”; body “Underhållsteamet tog fram kategorierna”.** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team itself designed the categories used in the repair log. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not itself design the categories used in the repair log. Support: S7 and Q1. “Själva” preserves customer authorship without asserting that Svale had no implementation role. Supported.

5. **Standfirst: “Underhållsansvariga Maya Lind”.** Proposition: Maya Lind is the customer's maintenance supervisor. Negation: Maya Lind is not the customer's maintenance supervisor. Support: Q0. The Swedish role description is a supported ordinary rendering of this role, without adding a higher rank or a new responsibility. Supported.

6. **Standfirst: “Maya Lind skulle göra om försöket”; final quotation “Jag skulle välja att göra om försöket”.** Proposition: Lind says that she would choose to undertake the trial again. Negation: Lind does not say that she would choose to undertake the trial again. Support: Q3 states that exact qualified preference. Neither passage asserts a scheduled repeat trial. Supported.

7. **Standfirst: “men avsätta mer tid för förberedelser”; subheading “Lind skulle avsätta mer tid för förberedelser”.** Proposition: Lind's preference for another trial includes allowing more preparation time than before. Negation: Lind's preference for another trial does not include allowing more preparation time than before. Support: Q3 specifies an extra week; S15 describes this as her actual qualified assessment. The general paraphrase preserves the reservation, and the body supplies its exact size. Supported.

8. **Standfirst: “Något beslut om att utöka försöket har ännu inte fattats.”** Proposition: At the time described, the team has not yet decided whether to expand the trial. Negation: At the time described, the team has already decided whether to expand the trial. Support: S16 says that the team “will decide after checking” the larger-repair categories. It is this expressly future decision, not simply the lack of expansion, that excludes the negation. Supported.

9. **“Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter.”** Proposition: Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. Negation: Elm Quay Housing does not manage 640 flats. Support: S1. Supported.

10. **“Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl separat.”** Proposition: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and emailed repair reports were stored separately. Negation: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and emailed repair reports were not stored separately. Support: S3 in the repair-log context established by S2. No unsupported claim of lost reports or customer incompetence is added. Supported.

11. **“I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam logg.”** Proposition: In September 2025, Elm Quay Housing's own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log. Negation: In September 2025, Elm Quay Housing's own maintenance team did not decide to trial a shared repair log. Support: S2 supplies date, ownership, actor and decision. This sentence does not independently assert an exact trial start date. Supported.

12. **“Försöket pågick i åtta veckor.”** Proposition: The trial lasted eight weeks. Negation: The trial did not last eight weeks. Support: S9. Supported.

13. **Quotation: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort.”** Proposition: Lind says that her team wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. Negation: Lind does not say that her team wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. Support: Q1, with the team referent settled by S4 and S7. The relative chronology conveyed by “redan” is in “already”. The quotation asserts an intention, not proof that every evening worker actually saw every morning action. Supported.

14. **Quotation: “Kategorierna var våra”.** Proposition: Lind says that the categories belonged to her team's work and were the team's own categories. Negation: Lind does not say that the categories were her team's own categories. Support: Q1 directly and S7 for the category-design context. This is attribution of category ownership/authorship, not an invented legal intellectual-property claim. Supported.

15. **Quotation: “Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”.** Proposition: Lind says that Svale helped her team put its categories into the repair log. Negation: Lind does not say that Svale helped her team put its categories into the repair log. Support: Q1, with “them” and “dem” both referring to categories. Supported.

16. **“berättar Maya Lind i en mejlintervju”.** Proposition: Maya Lind supplied the quoted remarks in an email interview. Negation: Maya Lind did not supply the quoted remarks in an email interview. Support: Q0 identifies the interviewee and S18 states that all interviews occurred by email. No physical encounter, remembered dialogue or observable emotion is manufactured. Supported.

17. **“Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa statusen för varje reparation.”** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could display each repair's status. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not choose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could display each repair's status. Support: S5. The sentence preserves sequence and the question tested; it does not claim that a supplier comparison demonstrated superiority. Supported.

18. **“Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.”** Proposition: The supplied case material contains no comparison with another supplier. Negation: The supplied case material contains a comparison with another supplier. Support: S6, together with the complete supplied package. The draft limits this absence to the material and does not claim that the customer never compared suppliers. Supported.

19. **“behöll möjligheten för de boende att felanmäla via telefon”.** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team kept telephone repair reporting available to residents during the trial. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not keep telephone repair reporting available to residents during the trial. Support: S7. Supported.

20. **“Svale konfigurerade loggen”.** Proposition: Svale configured the repair log for the trial. Negation: Svale did not configure the repair log for the trial. Support: S8. Supported.

21. **“utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen”.** Proposition: Svale trained six staff over two training sessions. Negation: Svale did not train six staff over two training sessions. Support: S8 supplies both numbers and the activity. The draft does not say there were twelve trainees or specify session duration. Supported.

22. **“För Lind gav arbetet en erfarenhet att ta med till nästa byggnad”.** Proposition: Lind's account of the category work includes an experience that informs her stated preparation choice for the next building. Negation: Lind's account of the category work includes no experience informing her stated preparation choice for the next building. Support: Q2 expressly connects the time spent agreeing categories to setting aside “that time” before the next building starts. This introductory characterisation attributes the lesson to Lind; it neither invents an emotion nor asserts that expansion is approved. Supported.

23. **Quotation: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första felanmälningarna.”** Proposition: Lind says that her team spent more time agreeing the categories than entering the first repair reports. Negation: Lind does not say that her team spent more time agreeing the categories than entering the first repair reports. Support: Q2. The comparison retains its two activities and its restriction to the first reports, without creating a measured duration. Supported.

24. **Quotation: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.”** Proposition: Lind says that she would reserve the time needed to agree the categories before work with the trial/log begins in the next building. Negation: Lind does not say that she would reserve the time needed to agree the categories before work with the trial/log begins in the next building. Support: Q2 (“that time”, “before the next building starts”), interpreted within S2 and S16. This preserves the source's contextual building-as-activity shorthand and hypothetical “would”. It does not state that another building has already started or has been approved. Supported.

25. **Subheading: “Kortare tid till tilldelning under försöket”.** Proposition: In the trial, the reported report-to-assignment time was shorter than in the comparison period, as measured by the median identified in the section. Negation: In the trial, the reported report-to-assignment time was not shorter than in the comparison period, as measured by that median. Support: S12's two-versus-three working days establishes the decrease. The heading uses assignment, not completion, and contains no causal verb or supplier agency. Its section immediately states the median, the comparison and the limitation. Supported.

26. **“Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025”.** Proposition: Elm Quay has an internal trial note dated 4 December 2025. Negation: Elm Quay does not have an internal trial note dated 4 December 2025. Support: S10. “Elm Quay” is an unambiguous shortened customer name. Supported.

27. **“Enligt … registrerades 31 felanmälningar.”** Proposition: Elm Quay's internal trial note dated 4 December 2025 says 31 repair reports were entered for the trial, within the exclusions stated immediately afterward. Negation: Elm Quay's internal trial note dated 4 December 2025 does not say 31 repair reports were entered for the trial within those exclusions. Support: S10 and S11. The draft does not present the note as independent validation or call the count high or low. Supported.

28. **“Akuta ärenden … ingår inte i underlaget.”** Proposition: The trial note's reporting/measurement material excludes emergencies. Negation: The trial note's reporting/measurement material includes emergencies. Support: S11. “Underlaget” here is locally the note's trial material; it does not deny the existence of emergency work. Supported.

29. **“arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte i underlaget”.** Proposition: The trial note's reporting/measurement material excludes work ordered before the trial. Negation: The trial note's reporting/measurement material includes work ordered before the trial. Support: S11. The modifier “före försöket” attaches to ordering, exactly as in the source; it has not become a restriction on when work finished. Supported.

30. **“Mediantiden från felanmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket”.** Proposition: Within the trial note's stated reporting scope, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial. Negation: Within that scope, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was not two working days during the trial. Support: S10–S12. The full metric, unit, period and exclusions are preserved. Supported.

31. **“jämfört med tre under den föregående åttaveckorsperioden”.** Proposition: Within the reported comparison, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was three working days in the eight-week period preceding the trial. Negation: Within that comparison, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was not three working days in the eight-week period preceding the trial. Support: S12. “Median”, “from report to assignment” and “working days” carry across the coordination; none is dropped in this reconstructed proposition. Supported.

32. **“Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna.”** Proposition: The trial period and preceding eight-week comparison period had different workloads. Negation: Those two periods did not have different workloads. Support: S13. No direction or magnitude of the workload difference is added. Supported.

33. **“Anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.”** Proposition: The internal note expressly does not attribute the observed median assignment-time difference to the software. Negation: It is not the case that the internal note expressly does not attribute that difference to the software. Support: S13 uses the same explicit non-attribution. The proposition concerns what the note attributes; it does not claim that the software is known to have had no effect. Supported.

34. **“Mätningen gäller alltså tiden tills ett ärende tilldelades, inte tills reparationen var klar.”** Proposition: The time measurement described measures report-to-assignment time, not repair-completion time. Negation: The time measurement described is not a report-to-assignment measurement distinct from repair-completion time. Support: S12 names the assignment endpoint and S14 states that there are no completion-time measurements. This clarification does not imply an unmeasured completion result. Supported.

35. **“Det saknas mätningar av kostnader”.** Proposition: The supplied trial evidence contains no cost measurements. Negation: The supplied trial evidence contains cost measurements. Support: S14. In the immediate discussion of the note and its measurements, this is an evidence-availability claim, not a claim that costs did not change. Supported.

36. **“[Det saknas mätningar av] hur nöjda de boende var”.** Proposition: The supplied trial evidence contains no resident-satisfaction measurements. Negation: The supplied trial evidence contains resident-satisfaction measurements. Support: S14. No resident sentiment is invented. Supported.

37. **“[Det saknas mätningar av] tiden till slutförd reparation”.** Proposition: The supplied trial evidence contains no repair-completion-time measurements. Negation: The supplied trial evidence contains repair-completion-time measurements. Support: S14. Supported.

38. **“Linds egen bedömning av försöket rymmer ett förbehåll”.** Proposition: The following assessment is Lind's own qualified assessment of the trial. Negation: The following assessment is not Lind's own qualified assessment of the trial. Support: S15 explicitly supplies both ownership and qualification; Q3 supplies the reservation. The draft does not infer Lind's assessment from the numerical results. Supported.

39. **Quotation: “Det hjälper oss att ha en samlad bild av felanmälningarna”.** Proposition: Lind says that having a single view of the repair reports helps her team. Negation: Lind does not say that having a single view of the repair reports helps her team. Support: Q3. This is a directly attributed practical assessment, with warranted affirmative certainty, not a measured causal claim about assignment times, costs or resident satisfaction. Supported.

40. **Quotation: “men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser”.** Proposition: Lind says that, although she would choose to do the trial again and finds the shared view helpful, she would allow one extra week for preparation. Negation: Lind does not say that, despite those positive assessments, she would allow one extra week for preparation. Support: Q3 preserves the conjunction, first-person preference and exact additional period. Supported.

41. **“Försöket har ännu inte utökats.”** Proposition: At the time described, the trial has not expanded. Negation: At the time described, the trial has expanded. Support: S16. Supported.

42. **“Teamet ska först kontrollera hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer och därefter fatta beslut.”** Proposition: Elm Quay's team will check how the categories work for larger repairs before deciding whether to expand the trial. Negation: Elm Quay's team will not check how the categories work for larger repairs before deciding whether to expand the trial. Support: S16 supplies future checking, larger-repair scope and decision order. In context “fatta beslut” refers to expansion, not a decision to purchase already made. The text leaves the eventual decision open. Supported.

43. **“För dig som vill läsa vidare finns [Svale Systems checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).”** Proposition: The supplied URL is an implementation checklist associated with Svale Systems, offered as an optional document for further reading. Negation: The supplied URL is not an implementation checklist associated with Svale Systems offered as an optional document for further reading. Support: B2 supplies the document type, exact URL and optional reading purpose, in the supplier-published brief B1. The conditional invitation makes no assertion that any particular reader wants to read it. It does not promise a consultation, trial or checklist results. Supported.

44. **Disclosure: “Den här kundberättelsen publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems.”** Proposition: This customer case is published as supplier material by Svale Systems, which is the supplier. Negation: This customer case is not published as supplier material by Svale Systems, the supplier. Support: B1 and S17. The journalistic form is not represented as editorial independence. Supported.

## Pronoun and person/number/gender accounting

This accounting separates reference from the grammatical or natural-person information expressed. None of these expressions requires an unsupported inference from Maya's name.

- **“själva”** in the standfirst: reflexive/intensive reference is the maintenance-team members acting as a group. It expresses their own agency and semantic plurality, without natural gender. S2 establishes a team, S7 its authorship and S8 explicitly establishes multiple trained staff. “Själva” is not an assertion that the supplier gave no help. Negation of the relevant assertion: the categories were not the team's own work. S7 and Q1 exclude it.
- **“Vi”** in quotations 1 and 2: first-person plural, including speaker Lind and a group; no natural-gender feature. The source has “We” in precisely both places. The team referent is settled by the interview and category context; person and number are independently supported by the actual first-person plural source wording. Negation: Lind's quoted “we” does not denote herself with a plural group in these statements. Q1 and Q2 exclude it.
- **“våra”** in quotation 1: first-person plural possessor; the categories are plural possessed items; no natural-gender assertion. Q1 “ours” independently supports the possessor person and number, and “categories” supports plurality of the possessed items. Negation: Lind does not present the plural categories as belonging to her first-person plural group. Q1 excludes it.
- **“oss”** in quotations 1 and 3: first-person plural object, speaker included, no natural gender. The source explicitly uses “us” in both passages. Negation: Lind does not describe her first-person plural group as recipient of Svale's assistance / beneficiary of the shared view, respectively. Q1 / Q3 exclude the corresponding negation.
- **“dem”** in quotation 1: third-person plural object referring to the categories, no natural gender. Q1's “them”, linked to “categories”, supplies reference and plurality separately. Negation: the quoted assistance concerns putting something other than the plural categories into the log. Q1 excludes it.
- **“Jag/jag”** in quotations 2 and 3: first-person singular Lind, no natural gender. Q2 and Q3 explicitly use “I”. Negation: the stated preparation choice / willingness to repeat / extra-week choice is not presented by Lind as her own individual choice. The respective source “I would” excludes each version of that negation.
- **“den tiden”** in quotation 2: singular demonstrative with Swedish common grammatical gender, referring to time for agreeing categories. It does not encode anybody's natural gender. Q2 “that time” supports the reference; time is a mass concept rather than a headcount. Negation: the time Lind would reserve is not the previously mentioned category-agreement time. Q2's linked sentences exclude it.
- **“sig”** in “Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig”: third-person reflexive in the Swedish expression for differed, carrying no independent number or natural-gender claim about a person. Its subject is workload. S13 supplies the asserted difference. Negation and support are recorded in entry 32.
- **“Det”** in “Det saknas mätningar”: impersonal syntactic subject, no person, number or natural-gender assertion concerning an entity. The evidence-absence claims are individually recorded in entries 35–37.
- **“Det”** in “Det hjälper oss att ha …”: anticipatory subject for the infinitive describing having one view. It adds no person or natural-gender information and makes no separate claim of an identified neuter object helping the team. Entry 39 captures the proposition supported by Q3.
- **“dig”** in the optional link sentence: singular second-person reader address, gender-neutral. It is a conditional invitation, not a factual assertion that there is exactly one reader or that the actual reader has a specified natural gender. B2 authorizes the optional reading invitation.
- **“Den här”** in the disclosure: singular demonstrative, common grammatical gender determined by “kundberättelsen”. The referent is the present text. B1 and S17 establish its supplier-publication status; no human gender is asserted.
- **“Något”** in the no-decision sentence: neuter indefinite determiner matching the grammatical gender of “beslut”. It contributes the negative existential claim about a decision in entry 8; no natural gender is involved.
- **“de boende”**: plural resident description, not a gendered personal pronoun. The source's “residents” expressly supports plurality. Neither phrase makes a natural-gender claim. Telephone availability and absent satisfaction measurements are supported by S7 and S14.
- **“Underhållsansvariga Maya Lind”**: this role adjective's -a form is not an independent assertion of female natural gender; Swedish uses this form without restricting the named person to a natural gender. The role is supported by Q0. The draft otherwise avoids “hon”, “han”, “hennes” and “hans”. In any event, the source itself calls the final quotation “Her final quotation”, so female reference would not depend solely on the name.
- **“Linds”, “Elm Quays”, “bolagets”, “Svale Systems”** possessive/naming constructions: these are named or nominal references, not gendered possessive pronouns. They add no natural-gender information. The customer/team relationship is explicit in S2; the note ownership is explicit in S10; Lind's assessment ownership is explicit in S15.

## Translated quotation comparison

### Quotation 1

Source: Q1. Draft: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”.

Meaning, intention, actor roles and relative time are preserved: wanted, evening shift, morning work already done, customer-owned categories and Svale's assistance. The distinction between the customer's category work and supplier implementation survives. “Ville … skulle se” and “hjälpte oss att lägga in” are idiomatic Swedish speech. “Kategorierna var våra” retains the speaker's succinct ownership emphasis. The speech dash marks an interview quotation, while the attribution accurately identifies email as its medium. No translation finding.

### Quotation 2

Source: Q2. Draft: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första felanmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.”

The comparative experience remains about category agreement versus entering the first reports; “mer tid” has not become a numerical measurement or a complaint about the supplier. “Skulle” preserves the speaker's conditional personal recommendation. “Den tiden” preserves the backward reference to category work. “Nästa byggnad kommer i gång” retains the source's ordinary contextual shorthand for starting the activity in another building. The supplied trial context settles that referent, and the text immediately elsewhere makes clear that expansion has not happened and its decision is pending. No concrete linguistic obstruction or new assertion of building construction arises from this metonymy. The practical, conversational voice survives. No translation finding.

### Quotation 3

Source: Q3. Draft: “Jag skulle välja att göra om försöket. Det hjälper oss att ha en samlad bild av felanmälningarna, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.”

The source's affirmative but qualified endorsement remains personal and conditional: Lind would choose to repeat the trial, the shared view helps her team, and she would reserve an extra preparation week. “Göra om försöket” naturally means undertake the trial again in this context; it does not assert that the first trial failed or must be corrected. “En samlad bild” idiomatically expresses “one view”. The inserted anticipatory “Det” is Swedish syntax, not a new actor or cause. The conjunction “men” retains the reservation and the exact week survives. Nothing becomes a general recommendation of Svale or an inference from the recorded median. No translation finding.

## Findings and completion

Source-support findings: none. Each factual or attributed proposition has supplied support that rules out its precise negation in the stated scope. No source-compatible counterexample requiring a repair was found.

Translation findings: none. The three quotations preserve meaning, stance, certainty, relevant wording and an idiomatic practical voice. No repair is required on source-support or translation grounds.

Completion status: COMPLETE. Full draft accounted for, including headings, implications, attribution, numerical modifiers and qualifications, and pronoun person/number/natural-gender information. Unresolved findings: none.

- S18: “All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.”

## Complete proposition accounting

Each numbered entry gives the draft passage, a standalone meaning-equivalent proposition, its precise negation with subject and scope retained, and the supplied statement excluding that negation. Repeated appearances are listed together only where they express the same proposition. Reported intentions and opinions remain statements about the named person's or team's intentions and opinions; they are not converted into objective efficacy claims. The propositions drawn from translated quotations retain their attribution to Lind.

1. **Title: “Elm Quay fick en gemensam överblick över felanmälningarna”.** Proposition: Elm Quay obtained a shared view of the repair reports in the trial. Negation: Elm Quay did not obtain a shared view of the repair reports in the trial. Support: S2 establishes the shared log and Q3 explicitly describes the customer as having one view of the reports. Together these rule out the negation. The title does not assert that the software caused a performance improvement.

2. **Standfirst: “Elm Quay Housing testade en gemensam logg för felanmälningar i två byggnader.”** Proposition: Elm Quay Housing trialled a shared repair-report log in two buildings. Negation: Elm Quay Housing did not trial a shared repair-report log in two buildings. Support: S2 identifies the trial, customer, shared log and two-building scope; S9 and S10 establish that the intended trial took place. Supported.

3. **Standfirst: “Underhållsteamet ville ge olika arbetsskift tillgång till samma information”.** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team wanted staff on different shifts to have access to the same information. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not want staff on different shifts to have access to the same information. Support: S4 states that intention. This does not claim independently measured information access or universal use. Supported.

4. **Standfirst: “utformade själva kategorierna”; subheading “Teamet utformade kategorierna”; body “Underhållsteamet tog fram kategorierna”.** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team itself designed the categories used in the repair log. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not itself design the categories used in the repair log. Support: S7 and Q1. “Själva” preserves customer authorship without asserting that Svale had no implementation role. Supported.

5. **Standfirst: “Underhållsansvariga Maya Lind”.** Proposition: Maya Lind is the customer's maintenance supervisor. Negation: Maya Lind is not the customer's maintenance supervisor. Support: Q0. The Swedish role description is a supported ordinary rendering of this role, without adding a higher rank or a new responsibility. Supported.

6. **Standfirst: “Maya Lind skulle göra om försöket”; final quotation “Jag skulle välja att göra om försöket”.** Proposition: Lind says that she would choose to undertake the trial again. Negation: Lind does not say that she would choose to undertake the trial again. Support: Q3 states that exact qualified preference. Neither passage asserts a scheduled repeat trial. Supported.

7. **Standfirst: “men avsätta mer tid för förberedelser”; subheading “Lind skulle avsätta mer tid för förberedelser”.** Proposition: Lind's preference for another trial includes allowing more preparation time than before. Negation: Lind's preference for another trial does not include allowing more preparation time than before. Support: Q3 specifies an extra week; S15 describes this as her actual qualified assessment. The general paraphrase preserves the reservation, and the body supplies its exact size. Supported.

8. **Standfirst: “Något beslut om att utöka försöket har ännu inte fattats.”** Proposition: At the time described, the team has not yet decided whether to expand the trial. Negation: At the time described, the team has already decided whether to expand the trial. Support: S16 says that the team “will decide after checking” the larger-repair categories. It is this expressly future decision, not simply the lack of expansion, that excludes the negation. Supported.

9. **“Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter.”** Proposition: Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. Negation: Elm Quay Housing does not manage 640 flats. Support: S1. Supported.

10. **“Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl separat.”** Proposition: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and emailed repair reports were stored separately. Negation: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and emailed repair reports were not stored separately. Support: S3 in the repair-log context established by S2. No unsupported claim of lost reports or customer incompetence is added. Supported.

11. **“I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam logg.”** Proposition: In September 2025, Elm Quay Housing's own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log. Negation: In September 2025, Elm Quay Housing's own maintenance team did not decide to trial a shared repair log. Support: S2 supplies date, ownership, actor and decision. This sentence does not independently assert an exact trial start date. Supported.

12. **“Försöket pågick i åtta veckor.”** Proposition: The trial lasted eight weeks. Negation: The trial did not last eight weeks. Support: S9. Supported.

13. **Quotation: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort.”** Proposition: Lind says that her team wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. Negation: Lind does not say that her team wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. Support: Q1, with the team referent settled by S4 and S7. The relative chronology conveyed by “redan” is in “already”. The quotation asserts an intention, not proof that every evening worker actually saw every morning action. Supported.

14. **Quotation: “Kategorierna var våra”.** Proposition: Lind says that the categories belonged to her team's work and were the team's own categories. Negation: Lind does not say that the categories were her team's own categories. Support: Q1 directly and S7 for the category-design context. This is attribution of category ownership/authorship, not an invented legal intellectual-property claim. Supported.

15. **Quotation: “Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”.** Proposition: Lind says that Svale helped her team put its categories into the repair log. Negation: Lind does not say that Svale helped her team put its categories into the repair log. Support: Q1, with “them” and “dem” both referring to categories. Supported.

16. **“berättar Maya Lind i en mejlintervju”.** Proposition: Maya Lind supplied the quoted remarks in an email interview. Negation: Maya Lind did not supply the quoted remarks in an email interview. Support: Q0 identifies the interviewee and S18 states that all interviews occurred by email. No physical encounter, remembered dialogue or observable emotion is manufactured. Supported.

17. **“Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa statusen för varje reparation.”** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could display each repair's status. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not choose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could display each repair's status. Support: S5. The sentence preserves sequence and the question tested; it does not claim that a supplier comparison demonstrated superiority. Supported.

18. **“Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.”** Proposition: The supplied case material contains no comparison with another supplier. Negation: The supplied case material contains a comparison with another supplier. Support: S6, together with the complete supplied package. The draft limits this absence to the material and does not claim that the customer never compared suppliers. Supported.

19. **“behöll möjligheten för de boende att felanmäla via telefon”.** Proposition: Elm Quay's maintenance team kept telephone repair reporting available to residents during the trial. Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance team did not keep telephone repair reporting available to residents during the trial. Support: S7. Supported.

20. **“Svale konfigurerade loggen”.** Proposition: Svale configured the repair log for the trial. Negation: Svale did not configure the repair log for the trial. Support: S8. Supported.

21. **“utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen”.** Proposition: Svale trained six staff over two training sessions. Negation: Svale did not train six staff over two training sessions. Support: S8 supplies both numbers and the activity. The draft does not say there were twelve trainees or specify session duration. Supported.

22. **“För Lind gav arbetet en erfarenhet att ta med till nästa byggnad”.** Proposition: Lind's account of the category work includes an experience that informs her stated preparation choice for the next building. Negation: Lind's account of the category work includes no experience informing her stated preparation choice for the next building. Support: Q2 expressly connects the time spent agreeing categories to setting aside “that time” before the next building starts. This introductory characterisation attributes the lesson to Lind; it neither invents an emotion nor asserts that expansion is approved. Supported.

23. **Quotation: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första felanmälningarna.”** Proposition: Lind says that her team spent more time agreeing the categories than entering the first repair reports. Negation: Lind does not say that her team spent more time agreeing the categories than entering the first repair reports. Support: Q2. The comparison retains its two activities and its restriction to the first reports, without creating a measured duration. Supported.

24. **Quotation: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.”** Proposition: Lind says that she would reserve the time needed to agree the categories before work with the trial/log begins in the next building. Negation: Lind does not say that she would reserve the time needed to agree the categories before work with the trial/log begins in the next building. Support: Q2 (“that time”, “before the next building starts”), interpreted within S2 and S16. This preserves the source's contextual building-as-activity shorthand and hypothetical “would”. It does not state that another building has already started or has been approved. Supported.

25. **Subheading: “Kortare tid till tilldelning under försöket”.** Proposition: In the trial, the reported report-to-assignment time was shorter than in the comparison period, as measured by the median identified in the section. Negation: In the trial, the reported report-to-assignment time was not shorter than in the comparison period, as measured by that median. Support: S12's two-versus-three working days establishes the decrease. The heading uses assignment, not completion, and contains no causal verb or supplier agency. Its section immediately states the median, the comparison and the limitation. Supported.

26. **“Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025”.** Proposition: Elm Quay has an internal trial note dated 4 December 2025. Negation: Elm Quay does not have an internal trial note dated 4 December 2025. Support: S10. “Elm Quay” is an unambiguous shortened customer name. Supported.

27. **“Enligt … registrerades 31 felanmälningar.”** Proposition: Elm Quay's internal trial note dated 4 December 2025 says 31 repair reports were entered for the trial, within the exclusions stated immediately afterward. Negation: Elm Quay's internal trial note dated 4 December 2025 does not say 31 repair reports were entered for the trial within those exclusions. Support: S10 and S11. The draft does not present the note as independent validation or call the count high or low. Supported.

28. **“Akuta ärenden … ingår inte i underlaget.”** Proposition: The trial note's reporting/measurement material excludes emergencies. Negation: The trial note's reporting/measurement material includes emergencies. Support: S11. “Underlaget” here is locally the note's trial material; it does not deny the existence of emergency work. Supported.

29. **“arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte i underlaget”.** Proposition: The trial note's reporting/measurement material excludes work ordered before the trial. Negation: The trial note's reporting/measurement material includes work ordered before the trial. Support: S11. The modifier “före försöket” attaches to ordering, exactly as in the source; it has not become a restriction on when work finished. Supported.

30. **“Mediantiden från felanmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket”.** Proposition: Within the trial note's stated reporting scope, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial. Negation: Within that scope, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was not two working days during the trial. Support: S10–S12. The full metric, unit, period and exclusions are preserved. Supported.

31. **“jämfört med tre under den föregående åttaveckorsperioden”.** Proposition: Within the reported comparison, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was three working days in the eight-week period preceding the trial. Negation: Within that comparison, the median elapsed time from report to assignment was not three working days in the eight-week period preceding the trial. Support: S12. “Median”, “from report to assignment” and “working days” carry across the coordination; none is dropped in this reconstructed proposition. Supported.

32. **“Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna.”** Proposition: The trial period and preceding eight-week comparison period had different workloads. Negation: Those two periods did not have different workloads. Support: S13. No direction or magnitude of the workload difference is added. Supported.

33. **“Anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.”** Proposition: The internal note expressly does not attribute the observed median assignment-time difference to the software. Negation: It is not the case that the internal note expressly does not attribute that difference to the software. Support: S13 uses the same explicit non-attribution. The proposition concerns what the note attributes; it does not claim that the software is known to have had no effect. Supported.

34. **“Mätningen gäller alltså tiden tills ett ärende tilldelades, inte tills reparationen var klar.”** Proposition: The time measurement described measures report-to-assignment time, not repair-completion time. Negation: The time measurement described is not a report-to-assignment measurement distinct from repair-completion time. Support: S12 names the assignment endpoint and S14 states that there are no completion-time measurements. This clarification does not imply an unmeasured completion result. Supported.

35. **“Det saknas mätningar av kostnader”.** Proposition: The supplied trial evidence contains no cost measurements. Negation: The supplied trial evidence contains cost measurements. Support: S14. In the immediate discussion of the note and its measurements, this is an evidence-availability claim, not a claim that costs did not change. Supported.

36. **“[Det saknas mätningar av] hur nöjda de boende var”.** Proposition: The supplied trial evidence contains no resident-satisfaction measurements. Negation: The supplied trial evidence contains resident-satisfaction measurements. Support: S14. No resident sentiment is invented. Supported.

37. **“[Det saknas mätningar av] tiden till slutförd reparation”.** Proposition: The supplied trial evidence contains no repair-completion-time measurements. Negation: The supplied trial evidence contains repair-completion-time measurements. Support: S14. Supported.

38. **“Linds egen bedömning av försöket rymmer ett förbehåll”.** Proposition: The following assessment is Lind's own qualified assessment of the trial. Negation: The following assessment is not Lind's own qualified assessment of the trial. Support: S15 explicitly supplies both ownership and qualification; Q3 supplies the reservation. The draft does not infer Lind's assessment from the numerical results. Supported.

39. **Quotation: “Det hjälper oss att ha en samlad bild av felanmälningarna”.** Proposition: Lind says that having a single view of the repair reports helps her team. Negation: Lind does not say that having a single view of the repair reports helps her team. Support: Q3. This is a directly attributed practical assessment, with warranted affirmative certainty, not a measured causal claim about assignment times, costs or resident satisfaction. Supported.

40. **Quotation: “men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser”.** Proposition: Lind says that, although she would choose to do the trial again and finds the shared view helpful, she would allow one extra week for preparation. Negation: Lind does not say that, despite those positive assessments, she would allow one extra week for preparation. Support: Q3 preserves the conjunction, first-person preference and exact additional period. Supported.

41. **“Försöket har ännu inte utökats.”** Proposition: At the time described, the trial has not expanded. Negation: At the time described, the trial has expanded. Support: S16. Supported.

42. **“Teamet ska först kontrollera hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer och därefter fatta beslut.”** Proposition: Elm Quay's team will check how the categories work for larger repairs before deciding whether to expand the trial. Negation: Elm Quay's team will not check how the categories work for larger repairs before deciding whether to expand the trial. Support: S16 supplies future checking, larger-repair scope and decision order. In context “fatta beslut” refers to expansion, not a decision to purchase already made. The text leaves the eventual decision open. Supported.

43. **“För dig som vill läsa vidare finns [Svale Systems checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).”** Proposition: The supplied URL is an implementation checklist associated with Svale Systems, offered as an optional document for further reading. Negation: The supplied URL is not an implementation checklist associated with Svale Systems offered as an optional document for further reading. Support: B2 supplies the document type, exact URL and optional reading purpose, in the supplier-published brief B1. The conditional invitation makes no assertion that any particular reader wants to read it. It does not promise a consultation, trial or checklist results. Supported.

44. **Disclosure: “Den här kundberättelsen publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems.”** Proposition: This customer case is published as supplier material by Svale Systems, which is the supplier. Negation: This customer case is not published as supplier material by Svale Systems, the supplier. Support: B1 and S17. The journalistic form is not represented as editorial independence. Supported.

## Pronoun and person/number/gender accounting

This accounting separates reference from the grammatical or natural-person information expressed. None of these expressions requires an unsupported inference from Maya's name.

- **“själva”** in the standfirst: reflexive/intensive reference is the maintenance-team members acting as a group. It expresses their own agency and semantic plurality, without natural gender. S2 establishes a team, S7 its authorship and S8 explicitly establishes multiple trained staff. “Själva” is not an assertion that the supplier gave no help. Negation of the relevant assertion: the categories were not the team's own work. S7 and Q1 exclude it.
- **“Vi”** in quotations 1 and 2: first-person plural, including speaker Lind and a group; no natural-gender feature. The source has “We” in precisely both places. The team referent is settled by the interview and category context; person and number are independently supported by the actual first-person plural source wording. Negation: Lind's quoted “we” does not denote herself with a plural group in these statements. Q1 and Q2 exclude it.
- **“våra”** in quotation 1: first-person plural possessor; the categories are plural possessed items; no natural-gender assertion. Q1 “ours” independently supports the possessor person and number, and “categories” supports plurality of the possessed items. Negation: Lind does not present the plural categories as belonging to her first-person plural group. Q1 excludes it.
- **“oss”** in quotations 1 and 3: first-person plural object, speaker included, no natural gender. The source explicitly uses “us” in both passages. Negation: Lind does not describe her first-person plural group as recipient of Svale's assistance / beneficiary of the shared view, respectively. Q1 / Q3 exclude the corresponding negation.
- **“dem”** in quotation 1: third-person plural object referring to the categories, no natural gender. Q1's “them”, linked to “categories”, supplies reference and plurality separately. Negation: the quoted assistance concerns putting something other than the plural categories into the log. Q1 excludes it.
- **“Jag/jag”** in quotations 2 and 3: first-person singular Lind, no natural gender. Q2 and Q3 explicitly use “I”. Negation: the stated preparation choice / willingness to repeat / extra-week choice is not presented by Lind as her own individual choice. The respective source “I would” excludes each version of that negation.
- **“den tiden”** in quotation 2: singular demonstrative with Swedish common grammatical gender, referring to time for agreeing categories. It does not encode anybody's natural gender. Q2 “that time” supports the reference; time is a mass concept rather than a headcount. Negation: the time Lind would reserve is not the previously mentioned category-agreement time. Q2's linked sentences exclude it.
- **“sig”** in “Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig”: third-person reflexive in the Swedish expression for differed, carrying no independent number or natural-gender claim about a person. Its subject is workload. S13 supplies the asserted difference. Negation and support are recorded in entry 32.
- **“Det”** in “Det saknas mätningar”: impersonal syntactic subject, no person, number or natural-gender assertion concerning an entity. The evidence-absence claims are individually recorded in entries 35–37.
- **“Det”** in “Det hjälper oss att ha …”: anticipatory subject for the infinitive describing having one view. It adds no person or natural-gender information and makes no separate claim of an identified neuter object helping the team. Entry 39 captures the proposition supported by Q3.
- **“dig”** in the optional link sentence: singular second-person reader address, gender-neutral. It is a conditional invitation, not a factual assertion that there is exactly one reader or that the actual reader has a specified natural gender. B2 authorizes the optional reading invitation.
- **“Den här”** in the disclosure: singular demonstrative, common grammatical gender determined by “kundberättelsen”. The referent is the present text. B1 and S17 establish its supplier-publication status; no human gender is asserted.
- **“Något”** in the no-decision sentence: neuter indefinite determiner matching the grammatical gender of “beslut”. It contributes the negative existential claim about a decision in entry 8; no natural gender is involved.
- **“de boende”**: plural resident description, not a gendered personal pronoun. The source's “residents” expressly supports plurality. Neither phrase makes a natural-gender claim. Telephone availability and absent satisfaction measurements are supported by S7 and S14.
- **“Underhållsansvariga Maya Lind”**: this role adjective's -a form is not an independent assertion of female natural gender; Swedish uses this form without restricting the named person to a natural gender. The role is supported by Q0. The draft otherwise avoids “hon”, “han”, “hennes” and “hans”. In any event, the source itself calls the final quotation “Her final quotation”, so female reference would not depend solely on the name.
- **“Linds”, “Elm Quays”, “bolagets”, “Svale Systems”** possessive/naming constructions: these are named or nominal references, not gendered possessive pronouns. They add no natural-gender information. The customer/team relationship is explicit in S2; the note ownership is explicit in S10; Lind's assessment ownership is explicit in S15.

## Translated quotation comparison

### Quotation 1

Source: Q1. Draft: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”.

Meaning, intention, actor roles and relative time are preserved: wanted, evening shift, morning work already done, customer-owned categories and Svale's assistance. The distinction between the customer's category work and supplier implementation survives. “Ville … skulle se” and “hjälpte oss att lägga in” are idiomatic Swedish speech. “Kategorierna var våra” retains the speaker's succinct ownership emphasis. The speech dash marks an interview quotation, while the attribution accurately identifies email as its medium. No translation finding.

### Quotation 2

Source: Q2. Draft: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första felanmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.”

The comparative experience remains about category agreement versus entering the first reports; “mer tid” has not become a numerical measurement or a complaint about the supplier. “Skulle” preserves the speaker's conditional personal recommendation. “Den tiden” preserves the backward reference to category work. “Nästa byggnad kommer i gång” retains the source's ordinary contextual shorthand for starting the activity in another building. The supplied trial context settles that referent, and the text immediately elsewhere makes clear that expansion has not happened and its decision is pending. No concrete linguistic obstruction or new assertion of building construction arises from this metonymy. The practical, conversational voice survives. No translation finding.

### Quotation 3

Source: Q3. Draft: “Jag skulle välja att göra om försöket. Det hjälper oss att ha en samlad bild av felanmälningarna, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.”

The source's affirmative but qualified endorsement remains personal and conditional: Lind would choose to repeat the trial, the shared view helps her team, and she would reserve an extra preparation week. “Göra om försöket” naturally means undertake the trial again in this context; it does not assert that the first trial failed or must be corrected. “En samlad bild” idiomatically expresses “one view”. The inserted anticipatory “Det” is Swedish syntax, not a new actor or cause. The conjunction “men” retains the reservation and the exact week survives. Nothing becomes a general recommendation of Svale or an inference from the recorded median. No translation finding.

## Findings and completion

Source-support findings: none. Each factual or attributed proposition has supplied support that rules out its precise negation in the stated scope. No source-compatible counterexample requiring a repair was found.

Translation findings: none. The three quotations preserve meaning, stance, certainty, relevant wording and an idiomatic practical voice. No repair is required on source-support or translation grounds.

Completion status: COMPLETE. Full draft accounted for, including headings, implications, attribution, numerical modifiers and qualifications, and pronoun person/number/natural-gender information. Unresolved findings: none.
"}

# Elm Quay fick en gemensam överblick över felanmälningarna

Elm Quay Housing testade en gemensam logg för felanmälningar i två byggnader. Underhållsteamet ville ge olika arbetsskift tillgång till samma information och utformade själva kategorierna. Underhållsansvariga Maya Lind skulle göra om försöket, men avsätta mer tid för förberedelser. Något beslut om att utöka försöket har ännu inte fattats.

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl separat. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam logg. Försöket pågick i åtta veckor.

– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen, berättar Maya Lind i en mejlintervju.

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa statusen för varje reparation. Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.

## Teamet utformade kategorierna

Underhållsteamet tog fram kategorierna och behöll möjligheten för de boende att felanmäla via telefon. Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen.

För Lind gav arbetet en erfarenhet att ta med till nästa byggnad:
